title: The War in Ukraine, Relations With China & Wider Geopolitics (With General David Petraeus)

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/The War in Ukraine, Relations With China & Wider Geopolitics (With General David Petraeus).docx

speakers: General David Petraeus (former US general and CIA director, KKR Global Institute chairman)
summary: January 2023 Money Maze interview on geopolitics. Petraeus assesses Ukraine, China, Iran, cyber and NATO, and for investors argues the world has moved from benign globalization to great-power rivalry where geopolitics constrains economics, with selective decoupling, just-in-case supply chains, and no near-term replacement for the dollar.

coverage.note: intro/bio; Ukraine strategic leadership framework (four tasks)
Ukraine battlefield, Russian losses, sanctions effect on Russia
how war ends, frozen conflict, pre-invasion call on Kyiv
Russian logistics and campaign design, Western arms supplies (military detail)
Ukrainian training, tactical nuclear weapons, Russian conscription (military detail)
negotiated settlement, neutrality idea, NATO accession
future of warfare: drones, hypersonics, if seen can be hit
cyber domain, NATO spending and unity
China deterrence, Afghanistan credibility, China demography question
China learning organization, zero COVID, Iran
cyberspace domain, Ukraine cyber resilience, zero trust
cyber info sharing, KKR clients, globalization to rivalry, export controls
KKR portfolio contingency planning, just-in-case logistics
China labor costs and robots, personal questions (Grant) with no method content
Grant at Shiloh, strategic leadership website, Kodak and Netflix (no method content)
plugs; closing summary: severe competition, higher fences, selective decoupling

completeness_estimate: 0.65 - the first reader caught the main geopolitical theses (strategic leadership, Ukraine war outlook, China learning, Iran indicators, dollar, globalization-to-rivalry, supply-chain shifts), but missed many supporting mechanisms and numbers (casualty ratios, Western aid scale, sanctions enforcement, Iran regime no-exit logic, Russia reserve figures, chip IP leverage, continuity-spend logic) and misattributed the cyber deterrence claim.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: a strategic leader has to perform four tasks well has to get the big Ideas the overall strategy right has to communicate all of that effectively
claims.claim: A strategic leader must do four tasks: get the big ideas right, communicate them, oversee implementation, and refine the strategy repeatedly; Petraeus judges Zelensky to have done this well and Putin poorly, which explains Ukraine taking the initiative.
claims.testable: no: leadership framework applied to war

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: a country one-third the size of Russia has a larger and more capable Army on the battlefield in Ukraine than does Russia
claims.claim: Ukraine's mobilization, training and equipment have given it a larger and more capable army in the field than Russia's, and the front has been static for months around Bakhmut with Russia taking heavy losses.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: Russia is sent from Central Casting when it comes to resisting sanctions because they have you know they're one of the top three gas oil and coal producers in the world
claims.claim: Russia is unusually well placed to resist sanctions as a top-three gas, oil and coal producer, yet sanctions and export controls are starting to bite: GDP fell perhaps about 5% rather than 10%, and over 1,200 Western companies left or scaled back.
claims.testable: partly: sanctions impact on GDP measurable

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: I don't think either country wants to have a new Frozen conflict as the term was after the Russians seized Crimea in 2014
claims.claim: A frozen conflict would leave Russia under sanctions and Ukraine under bombardment, so negotiations become possible only when Putin recognizes the war is unsustainable, with rebuilding and security guarantees needed afterwards.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: in an interview with the Atlantic uh magazine here in the U.S I said that Russia would not take Keith much less ever control it
claims.claim: The speaker's pre-invasion call that Russia would not take Kyiv rested on watching Ukrainian forces improve since 2014 through Western training, intelligence and anti-tank weapons.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: they have perhaps one quarter or one-fifth of the logistics infrastructure the organizational structure that we have that enables us to be expeditionary
claims.claim: Russian forces have good rail logistics but only a fraction of the off-rail logistics of Western armies and have not combined arms effects, so their offensives were ineptly planned.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: a tactical nuclear weapon as horrific as it may be and it's Crossing that threshold as significant as that is has a tactical effect
claims.claim: A tactical nuclear weapon would not reverse Russia's strategic situation because Ukraine out-mobilizes it, and Russian conscription is not going well.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: you don't get a vote on this anymore
claims.claim: The West's earlier caution to avoid provoking Putin failed; Ukraine neutrality or Crimea lease ideas floated before the invasion may be part of an eventual settlement, with a Marshall Plan and security guarantee; Finland and Sweden will join NATO.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: if it can be seen it can be hit if it can be hit it can be killed
claims.claim: Ukraine gives only glimpses of future war; with drones, long-range precision munitions and ubiquitous surveillance, big manned platforms (carriers, F-35s, tanks) become vulnerable, pushing militaries toward many small unmanned, algorithm-piloted systems.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: Germany which was not even at 1.5 percent of GDP being spent on defense all of a sudden Rockets to two percent and even has a 110 billion dollar equivalent for Readiness
claims.claim: Russia's invasion raised European defense spending (Germany from under 1.5% to above 2% of GDP plus a 110 billion fund), and NATO unity is at a post-Cold War high with Finland and Sweden joining; the US spends three to four times as much as the other NATO allies combined.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: deterrence is a function of two elements it's a potential adversaries perception of your capabilities on the one hand and we have to transform those
claims.claim: Deterrence rests on credible capabilities and clear will to use them; doubt about US will after Afghanistan and the Syria red line weakens it, while the US response on Ukraine restored credibility. Competition with China must be managed so it does not become conflict.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: is China a learning organization because at least from an outside perspective one can ask was Zero covet a wise domestic policy
claims.claim: China reversed zero-COVID, which Petraeus reads as a sign it can learn and might also reverse wolf-warrior diplomacy, economic coercion (Australia) and border clashes; this would allow a more constructive relationship despite severe competition.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: this kind of indicator is just not there yet it's not impossible that it could emerge
claims.claim: Regime change in Iran would show up as indicators like oil workers striking (as in 1979) or the security forces refusing to kill protesters (Egypt 2011); these are absent, so the regime probably is not overthrown soon, and Western support must be covert to avoid helping the regime.
claims.indicator: oil worker strikes, security force defection
claims.conditions: large loyal security forces (Basij over 2 million)

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: there's no sign I don't think of true displacement of the dollar as the currency through which much of trade uh is done
claims.claim: Freezing Russian reserves may cause tactical diversification (euro, pound, yuan) but no true displacement of the dollar, because no alternative offers rule of law, transparency and stability; even China did not unfreeze or break export controls.
claims.conditions: no alternative as stable and trusted

claims.speaker: Simon (host)
claims.quote: do you believe that the major players are acting in a similar way to mutualists just show destruction in the Cold War because they have the capability to shut down enemies critical infrastructure
claims.claim: Cyber deterrence resembles mutual assured destruction only in theory: cyber capabilities are less predictable than nuclear weapons and untested until used.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker and quote: Simon only asks whether major powers behave as in Cold War mutually assured destruction (relaying a question from Rob Rooney). The content of the claim (cyber is less predictable than nuclear weapons, untested until used, but still has some deterrent effect) is David Petraeus's answer.
correction.fix: David Petraeus: cyber deterrence is a theory the powers should demonstrate; capabilities are known only partly and are untested until used, so cyber is far less precise than a nuclear warhead whose yield and target are known, yet the mutual fear of each other's capabilities has some deterrent effect.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: there was a huge fear that Russia would completely shut down Ukraine would completely disable their telecommunications their access to the internet
claims.claim: Russia's large cyberattack on Ukraine largely failed because Ukraine improved cyber resilience with Western and Microsoft help; defense in cyber is hard because attackers need to succeed once, so firms need zero-trust, compartmentalized security and real-time threat sharing.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: we've gone from an era of benign globalization in which economics determined geopolitics
claims.claim: The world has moved from benign globalization where economics determined geopolitics to renewed great-power rivalry where geopolitics determines what is economically possible, constraining investment and trade.
claims.testable: partly: test regime split on cross-asset correlations

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it will be higher fences around fewer items rather than Many Many Items surrounded by less high fences
claims.claim: US export controls on advanced chips, fabrication equipment and IP will likely be more restrictions with higher fences around fewer items, affecting investment limits such as entity lists, dual-use technology and data flows.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: just in time Logistics no longer works in an era of pandemics in an area when entire regions of the biggest manufacturing country in the world are shut down
claims.claim: Firms are moving from just-in-time to just-in-case logistics (higher inventories, warehouses) and diversifying manufacturing from China to Vietnam, India and Southeast Asia, which has capacity limits.
claims.direction: more inventory, relocate away from China

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: We examined our European portfolio so what is our exposure to Russia and
claims.claim: Private-equity investors stress-tested portfolio exposure to Russia and Ukraine after 2014 and 2020 and put business-continuity plans in place, which paid off when the invasion came.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: you see the rise of the robots which means that you can actually bring something back to the United States
claims.claim: Rising Chinese labor costs and robotics lower the labor-cost gap so production can return to the US, Mexico or Canada, supporting reshoring.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: we are in a severe competition to use the term of our national security advisor without question but the cold war has implications that just aren't found here
claims.claim: The Cold War analogy fails because the US and China are each other's top-three trading partners; selective decoupling in critical technology is likely, not complete decoupling.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: they've taken at least six and maybe as much as eight or nine times the casualties in the first 10 or 11 months that they took in nearly 10 years in Afghanistan
claims.claim: Russian casualties in the first 10-11 months were at least six to nine times those of nearly ten years in Afghanistan (some estimates up to 100,000 versus about 13,000), yet Putin seems unconcerned, so battlefield losses alone do not force him to recognise the war as unsustainable.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: they just keep squeezing harder on all this trying to have avoid situations in which countries can circumvent various sanctions and Export controls
claims.claim: Sanctions and export controls are continually tightened to close circumvention routes through third countries, which is why Petraeus expects their economic bite on Russia to grow over time.
claims.testable: yes - Russian GDP and trade-diversion data

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it's very very intangible it's psychological as much as it is physical
claims.claim: When an army collapses is intangible and psychological as much as physical, so the timing of a Russian collapse cannot be read from material indicators; the West's lever is to supply Ukraine fully to hasten the moment Putin must decide.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: way over 130 howitzers for example 155 millimeter heavy a million rounds of of 155 millimeter Howitzer ammunition
claims.claim: Western support has scaled to over 130 heavy 155mm howitzers, about a million rounds of ammunition, and HIMARS with precision rockets (about 80 km range) plus Excalibur shells, material that came on top of Ukraine's own mobilisation.
claims.indicator: Western military aid quantities to Ukraine

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: the UK is publicly known his training units not just individual Soldiers the U.S is doing the same
claims.claim: Western allies train whole units and wargame offensives, not just individual soldiers, which raises Ukrainian effectiveness, although complex systems like Patriot and infantry fighting vehicles take time to field.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: when they did the last partial mobilization more Russian men left the country than reported to the recruiting station
claims.claim: Russia's partial mobilisation drove more men to emigrate than reported for service, an indicator of weak popular support and labour flight that undercuts its larger population as an advantage.
claims.indicator: emigration vs conscript reporting in Russia
claims.testable: partly - emigration estimates exist, conscript reporting is opaque

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: there could be various factors on the home front including ultimately perhaps at some point you know pressures to topple him or to challenge him
claims.claim: Russian domestic pressure, including a possible challenge to Putin, is one factor that could force the realisation that the war is unsustainable, which is the precondition for negotiations.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: now whether that is still possible in the domestic politics of the country 95 of whose citizens want to see all of Ukraine liberated
claims.claim: Pre-war ideas of neutrality or a Crimea lease may be hard to revive because about 95% of Ukrainians want all of Ukraine liberated, so Ukrainian domestic politics constrains any compromise.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: the human in the loop becomes the human who designed the algorithm and maybe pushes a button
claims.claim: Competition pushes towards autonomy: a force that keeps a human in each decision loop will lose to the opposing machine acting at machine speed, so the human role shifts to designing the algorithm and authorising it.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: in cyberspace a whole new Battlefield domain where there's war going on every day but where the intensity would be vastly greater
claims.claim: Cyberspace is a new battlefield domain where conflict is already daily and will intensify, aimed at disrupting the networks linking sensors, shooters and autonomous systems.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: pushing uh Finland and Sweden uh into seeking accession to Nato is very very important Geo strategically the Baltic becomes a NATO Lake now
claims.claim: Putin's invasion pushed Finland and Sweden into NATO, which is geostrategically important because it makes the Baltic a NATO lake and turns the Arctic into a new field of competition.
claims.conditions: accession completed (Hungary and Turkey were holding it up)

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: okay yeah let's see it do it but don't reorganize what you have now and create a new headquarters to oversee them
claims.claim: European defence autonomy is credible only if it adds real capabilities (additional battalions, cyber) rather than new headquarters, concepts or reorganisation, so spending outputs should be judged by capability.
claims.testable: partly - capability metrics can be tracked

claims.speaker: Simon (host)
claims.quote: the Chinese population going from 1.3 billion to not much more than 600 million by the end of the century
claims.claim: A World Economic Forum projection has China's population falling from 1.3 billion to little more than 600 million by 2100, a structural headwind raised in the question of whether Xi overestimates China's strength.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it was predictable that the death rate would be would Skyrocket and it will and I think It ultimately will surpass that of the United States
claims.claim: Reversing zero-COVID without mRNA vaccines and with weak elderly vaccination predictably produces a surge in Chinese COVID deaths that may ultimately exceed the US toll of over a million.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it's caused the EU to show the investment agreement it's caused a number of other countries to respond to that as well
claims.claim: Wolf-warrior diplomacy carried economic costs: it led the EU to shelve its investment agreement with China and prompted other countries to respond, so reversing it could restore investment ties.
claims.testable: partly - investment-flow data vs diplomacy episodes

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: they are unarmed they're largely unorganized I mean that's one of their strengths is that there's no key leadership that can be decapitated
claims.claim: Petraeus is more sceptical than Iran scholar Karim Sadjadpour, who now thinks the regime will fall: unarmed, leaderless protesters face an organised, armed Basij of over two million plus the Revolutionary Guards, so timing is uncertain.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it's not a case where if the supreme leader goes down they can all step back and retain their positions under the next leader
claims.claim: Iranian security forces have no exit like Egypt's army had when Mubarak fell (they would likely fall with the Supreme Leader), which lowers the chance of defection and raises the chance they fight on.
claims.conditions: regime where elite survival is tied to the leader

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: to have control of very powerful militias on the street so you have Street muscle and then you have control of a sufficient Block in the Parliament that you can block even veto anything that you don't like
claims.claim: Iran's playbook in Iraq and Syria is to replicate its Lebanon model: control powerful street militias plus a parliamentary bloc big enough to veto anything, giving influence without formal rule.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: going to sanction prove itself stash 600 billion dollars around the world including 200 billion in China and then every country throws those including China by the way
claims.claim: Russia held roughly $600 billion of reserves abroad, about $200 billion of it in China, and all countries including China froze them, showing that rule-of-law dollar assets were treated as safe and that the Russia-China partnership had limits.
claims.indicator: Russian central bank reserves held abroad; frozen reserves

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: very happy to exploit the moment and get yet further advantageous deals on natural gas or oil or what have you from Russia at Russia's moment of weakness
claims.claim: China exploits Russia's moment of weakness to obtain advantageous gas and oil deals while not breaching export controls in any meaningful way, a transactional partnership that has limits rather than being 'without limits'.
claims.indicator: Russian oil and gas export discounts to China
claims.direction: China buys Russian energy on better terms

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: this takes about roughly 85 discrete capabilities if you will applications
claims.claim: A proper zero-trust, managed cyber security solution takes roughly 85 discrete capabilities, so cyber security is a complex, multi-product spend; Petraeus sits on the board of the largest pure-play cyber services firm (caption: octave), owned by KKR, which also holds other cyber investments.
claims.testable: partly - spend data, though the 85-capability count is anecdotal

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: it takes hours sometimes days you've got to operate at machine speed not at telephone or individual alert speed
claims.claim: Real-time sharing of cyber threat information is the missing big idea because US Congress has been reluctant to compel prompt reporting (fiduciary and stock-price concerns), so alerts take hours or days rather than machine speed.
claims.conditions: mandatory reporting rules in the US

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: with machines made in Netherlands and Germany but all based on usip that is a very very substantial restriction
claims.claim: Although the most advanced chips are made in Taiwan and Korea with Dutch and German machines, everything rests on US intellectual property, so US export controls bind the whole semiconductor supply chain and are likely to widen.
claims.indicator: US export controls on advanced chips, fabrication equipment and IP
claims.testable: partly - rule changes are observable; impact on firms is testable event-study style

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: now you get into how do you apply that to specific relationships specific regions specific countries and ultimately to specific Industries and then ultimately specific investment opportunities
claims.claim: A top-down process: first accept the big regime shift (geopolitics now circumscribes economics), then apply it to specific relationships, regions, countries, industries and finally individual investments.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: we've never invested directly in companies in Russia and Ukraine but we have you know very substantial customers and actually numbers of workers thousands of uh in each country
claims.claim: Geopolitical exposure runs through indirect channels (customers and remote IT workers) even without direct investment, so exposure mapping must go beyond holdings to revenue and workforce dependence.
claims.indicator: portfolio-company revenue and workforce exposure to Russia and Ukraine

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: until it does people think gosh can we cut this cost I mean really do we actually need to this is uh something
claims.claim: Business-continuity and contingency spending looks like a cost to cut until a shock hits; the Ukraine invasion showed it was insurance with high value, so such spending should be protected.

claims.speaker: David Petraeus
claims.quote: the case of Kodak where they had you know 2 000 patents in digital photography but failed in that fourth task to make the new big idea digital rather than film
claims.claim: Kodak is the example of failing the fourth strategic-leadership task: it held about 2,000 digital-photography patents but did not make digital the big idea, while Netflix's Reed Hastings is cited as a model strategic leader.
